source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Oral iron generally being absorbed and utilized more quickly and far more reliably by the body than IV iron in clients who have chronic kidney disease","B":"Absorption of oral iron can be limited in CKD, and IV administration ensures more reliable iron delivery, particularly important for clients also receiving erythropoiesis-stimulating agents","C":"IV iron carrying fairly little established role in managing anemia related to chronic kidney disease in most clients receiving ongoing hemodialysis treatment sessions","D":"Oral iron generally having fairly few absorption limitations in clients who have chronic kidney disease compared with the general adult population"}}
source_row.rationale: IV iron is often preferred over oral iron in CKD because oral iron absorption can be limited in this population, and IV administration ensures more reliable iron delivery, particularly important for clients also receiving erythropoiesis-stimulating agents who need adequate iron stores for effective response.
